text:
ashley: Heads up — thinking about a quota-aware sampling mode for request/response telemetry. Right now a few long responses from some tenants burn our ingest quota and admins manually flip sampling off, which kills signal. Quick proposal and sanity check pls.

jonah: short q: what's the sampling rule?

ashley: sample by token budget, not by request count. idea: each tenant has a telemetry_token_budget (tokens/month). for a response of N tokens, sample with prob = min(1, target_budget_per_sample / N). big responses -> lower chance, small responses -> still likely sampled. Also: always redact before storage, and keep an encrypted inspect store for support when customer opts in.

maria: ok but if we downsample huge responses we might miss rare long-tail failures that only appear in big outputs. any stratification?

ashley: good call — add a "min_always_sample_rate" for >Xk token responses (eg 0.1%). plus an override if response contains error codes or stack traces -> force-sample.

lee: runtime concern: do this at the edge-scrubber so raw payload never leaves region. we should emit metrics: sampled_tokens, unsampled_tokens, forced_sample_count. also keep random seed per-tenant to avoid correlated drops.

devex: console UX notes: expose per-route "telemetry token burn estimator" and a canary slider for sampling rollouts. mock: "canary sampling: 5% -> 20% -> 100%" and a toggle for "inspect-mode (support access)" with audit log link.

legal: two immediate asks: 1) define exactly what goes into the inspect store (full payload? masked? derived data?) 2) retention defaults and customer consent text. hashed ids must use a per-tenant salt and documented rotation policy.

ashley: yes — plan: inline redaction first (heuristics + KV-mask). if still flagged and customer has inspect-mode enabled, store encrypted blob in inspect-store with metadata: route, request_id, truncated_prompt_hash, redaction_flags. retention default 30 days. sample config below: \n\n```yaml\ndynamic_sampler:\n  type: quota_aware\n  token_budget_per_month: 10000000 # tokens\n  target_budget_per_sample: 1000\n  min_always_sample_rate: 0.001 # 0.1% for huge responses\n  forced_sample_conditions:\n    - error_code_present\n    - contains_stack_trace\n  redact_policy: heuristics+kvmask\n  inspect_mode_enabled: true\n  inspect_retention_days: 30\n  per_tenant_salt_rotation_days: 90\n```\n\njonah: implementation note: do sampling drop decision before we compute/store embeddings or any downstream compute to save cost. also push this into the routing policy so tenants with reserved capacity have different defaults.

maria: i'll add a small test-suite of prompts that intentionally elicit PII to validate the redactor. will attach in the RFC.

lee: also recommend keeping a tiny fixed reservoir of very-large responses (~100/day across fleet) to ensure we capture long-tail patterns for model/regression detectors.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: applied canary config to route /v1/generate in prod at 1765123500 (5% sampling, quota-aware). watch privacy_hits, telemetry_burn_rate, large_response_error_rate.

ashley: thanks all — i'll file an RFC with the YAML above, a console mock, and a checklist for legal. @legal please ping here with contract language checklist.

legal: will do, aiming to respond EOD with allowed inspect-store fields and retention wording.

devex: quick UX follow-up: can we show "estimated monthly token burn" for each route in the UI before they flip anything? customers keep asking for that.

ashley: yep — add to RFC.

lee: :thumbsup:

maria: adding tests now.

jonah: I'll start an infra spike for edge-scrubber integration and randomness per-tenant.

ashley: awesome — closing this thread for now, RFC incoming.
